extracted.intended_audience: poets and literary critics; aspiring critics and writers of poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Didactic guidance on how to write poetry and how to judge (criticize) poetry fairly and well, blending rules of taste, morals of criticism, classical precedents, and stylistic advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your own reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sure yourself and your own reach to know; launch not beyond your depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics (and writers) should understand the limits of their genius, taste and learning and avoid attempting work beyond their capacity; 'mark that point where sense and dullness meet.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow nature as the standard
rubrics_metrics.description: First follow nature and your judgment frame by her just standard, which is still the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature is the unerring universal light and the test of art; rules are valid when they reflect natural expression—use nature as source and end of art; where rules conflict with nature they should be re-evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from the ancients / study Homer
rubrics_metrics.description: Be Homer's works your study and delight; know each ancient's proper character, his fable, subject, scope, religion, country, genius of his age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use great classical examples to form judgment and maxims; read ancient masters closely, compare texts with themselves, and let classical precedent inform critical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know when rules are merely methodized nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Those rules, of old discovered, not devised, are nature still, but nature methodized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that poetic rules derive from nature; treat rules as guides to achieve natural ends rather than arbitrary constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit rare, justified license
rubrics_metrics.description: Some lucky license answer to the full the intent proposed; that license is a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great wits may 'gloriously offend' and deviate from precepts when the deviation achieves the work's intent and has precedent; such transgression should be rare, necessary, and defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pedantry and false learning
rubrics_metrics.description: So by false learning is good sense defaced; some are bewildered in the maze of schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't let mere book-learning substitute for common sense; excessive scholasticism distorts judgment and spoils taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a practitioner before you teach
rubrics_metrics.description: Let such teach others who themselves excel, and censure freely, who have written well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should have experience of writing; authority in judgment comes from demonstrated skill in the art one critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid being half-learned (the 'half-formed witling')
rubrics_metrics.description: Those half-learned witlings... unfinished things one knows not what to call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Half-knowledge yields confused and pretentious criticism; avoid superficial learning that produces coxcombs and pretenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value total effect over isolated parts
rubrics_metrics.description: In wit, as nature, what affects our hearts is not the exactness of peculiar parts... but the joint force and full result of all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the overall effect ('the whole at once is bold and regular'), not merely discrete technicalities; a well-proportioned whole matters more than perfect parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge according to the author's intent
rubrics_metrics.description: In every work regard the writer's end, since none can compass more than they intend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether means and conduct are appropriate to the writer's aim; applause is due if intent is achieved despite trivial faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't be a nitpicking verbal critic
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglect the rules each verbal critic lays; for not to know some trifles is a praise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor verbal issues shouldn't dominate judgment; avoid making the whole depend on petty points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid judging solely by form/metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: But most by numbers judge a poet's song, and smooth or rough, with them is right or wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let equal syllables, smoothness or mechanical rhyme patterns be the sole criteria—music should serve sense; formal regularity alone doesn't equal merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: True ease comes from art, not chance
rubrics_metrics.description: True ease in writing comes from art, not chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effortless-sounding writing should be the product of craft and practice; techniques (rhythm, diction) should fit content—e.g., rough verse for tumult, smooth for softness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match style to subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Expression is the dress of thought; for different styles with different subjects sort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose language, diction and ornament appropriate to the subject's tone and scope; style should enhance thought, not obscure it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid false eloquence and excessive ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: False eloquence... Its gaudy colors spread on every place... All glares alike without distinction gay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware ornate words that hide lack of sense; ornament should not replace substance—'a vile conceit in pompous words' is unsuitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extremes in diction (neither too new nor too old)
rubrics_metrics.description: In words as fashions the same rule will hold, alike fantastic if too new or old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be the first to try the new merely for novelty, nor the last to drop obsolete fashions; balance between innovation and tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shun pride, malice and servility in judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Pride, malice, folly... A constant critic at the great man's board, to fetch and carry nonsense for my lord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid evaluative bias arising from pride, envy, faction, or slavish deference to status; judge works on merit, not on authorial rank or social influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of bandwagon and precedent-only reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ne'er advance a judgment of their own, but catch the spreading notion of the town.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't adopt the prevailing opinion without assessment; avoid reasoning solely by precedent or fashion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not judge author by name/status
rubrics_metrics.description: Some judge of authors' names not works, and then nor praise nor blame the writing, but the men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique the writing itself rather than the author's reputation; fame should not shield faults nor condemn merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be the first to praise true merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Be thou the first true merit to befriend; his praise is lost who stays till all commend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support genuine talent early rather than waiting for consensus; short modern fame requires timely praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid envy and petty rivalry
rubrics_metrics.description: Envy will merit, as its shade, pursue... But sense survived, when merry jests were past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let jealousy drive criticism; true merit persists beyond temporary attacks—critics should resist using a career as vehicle for spite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemn obscenity despite wit
rubrics_metrics.description: No pardon vile obscenity should find, though wit and art conspire to move your mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even cleverness does not excuse obscene content; dullness with obscenity is shameful and should be censured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be candid, truthful, and courteous
rubrics_metrics.description: In all you speak, let truth and candor shine; men must be taught as if you taught them not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speak truthfully but with good-breeding and tact; teach gently—'without good breeding truth is disapproved.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrain censure; be silent when unsure
rubrics_metrics.description: Be silent always, when you doubt your sense; and speak, though sure, with seeming diffidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncertain about a judgment, remain silent; when speaking, show humility; blunt, persistent assertion of error is fault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer advice generously but discreetly
rubrics_metrics.description: Be niggards of advice on no pretense; with mean complacence, ne'er betray your trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not hoard counsel; offer it when needed but do not betray confidence or flatter for gain; fear not anger of the wise when reproving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the 'bookful blockhead'—learn modestly
rubrics_metrics.description: The bookful blockhead ignorantly read, with loads of learned lumber in his head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading alone does not equal understanding; avoid critics who merely display quotations and assume superiority without genuine insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be unbiased, sincere, modestly bold and humane
rubrics_metrics.description: Unbiased, or by favor, or in spite, not dully prepossessed, nor blindly right; though learned, well-bred, and though well bred, sincere, modestly bold, and humanly severe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character sketch of the ideal critic: balanced judgment, humane severity, readiness to praise enemies' merits, and capacity to show faults to friends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use classical critical exemplars (Horace, Longinus, Quintilian)
rubrics_metrics.description: Horace still charms... Quintilian's copious work we find the justest rules and clearest method joined... Thee bold Longinus! all the Nine inspire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study classical critics as models of taste and method—Horace for graceful ease, Quintilian for method, Longinus for passion and the sublime.
